name: Souffle de Volaille
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: good white sauce made with butter, flour, milk, good chicken stock and a little cream
ingredients.originalText: good white sauce made with butter, flour, milk, good chicken stock and a little cream

instructions.text: Pound meat in a mortar (or pass twice through fine mincer), add gradually three ounces butter, four yolks and two whites of eggs.
Season to taste and then pass through a hair sieve.
Whip the remaining two whites of eggs to a stiff froth.
Half whip the cream and stir these in very gently to the chicken mixture.
Steam very gently in mould for three-quarters of an hour.
Turn out and serve with good white sauce made with butter, flour, milk, good chicken stock and a little cream.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Pound meat in a mortar (or pass twice through fine mincer), add gradually three ounces butter, four yolks and two whites of eggs.
2. Season to taste and then pass through a hair sieve.
3. Whip the remaining two whites of eggs to a stiff froth.
4. Half whip the cream and stir these in very gently to the chicken mixture.
5. Steam very gently in mould for three-quarters of an hour.
6. Turn out and serve with good white sauce made with butter, flour, milk, good chicken stock and a little cream.
